name: tonic
description: Tonic 0.14 reference gRPC implementation over Hyper/H2 with Prost and protobuf-tonic

upstream_pin.notes: Exact versions resolved in tests/interop/tonic/Cargo.lock; build with --locked

tonic-prost.description: End-to-end reference: tonic 0.14 transport with prost codec (tonic-interop binary)
tonic-prost.client_support_notes: No prost load generator exists; the matrix fails tonic-prost client cells explicitly instead of substituting the pbrs codec.

tonic-pbrs.description: Same-codec transport reference: tonic 0.14 transport with pbrs codec (rpc-bench --transport=tonic); isolates transport deltas from serialization

tonic.description: Legacy alias: server requires tonic-prost; client is always tonic-pbrs. Missing prost server fails rather than substituting another codec. Use explicit flavors for codec claims.

server.description: Tonic interop & benchmark server (from tests/interop/tonic or rpc-bench)

client.description: Tonic interop & benchmark client (from tests/interop/tonic or rpc-bench)

matching_configuration.cores: matched pinned cores; effective quota recorded per run
matching_configuration.http2_windows: 16 MiB native-matched windows on tonic-pbrs; tonic-interop server defaults on tonic-prost (see rpc-bench/peers/tonic-pbrs.json and tonic-prost.json)
matching_configuration.message_limits: 4 MiB worker body cap on tonic-pbrs; tonic-prost server defaults
matching_configuration.deadlines: 5 s worker deadline on tonic-pbrs; interop server defaults on tonic-prost
matching_configuration.handler_work: same TestService procedures and payloads as native on both flavors; codec is pbrs (tonic-pbrs) or prost (tonic-prost)

tls.reason: rpc-bench has no TLS for the tonic transport: tonic 0.14 TLS pulls a C crypto provider, conflicting with the pure-Rust dependency policy (QG-04). TLS cells touching tonic-pbrs/tonic-prost are unsupported with this reason, never silently plaintext.
